Bengaluru Settlement Needs Map
Bangalore Urban Programme · All-zone site assessment and the GBA proposal · updated 28 October 2026

What each settlement needs, what went to GBA, and what starts in Year 1

Every site from the all-zone assessment, placed in its GBA city corporation, with the 71 sites proposed to GBA on 28 October 2026 and the Year 1 earmarks. Start with the GBA proposal tab for the numbers in the note; use the other tabs to see how they were arrived at. It keeps the blocked and dropped sites and the reasoning. The shaded footprints under the dots are the settlements the programme’s partner teams have mapped and work in every day — the ground these assessments were made from and the ground the proposal speaks for. Switch the map to Satellite to see any site as it stands.

    Sites

    How priority and feasibility were assigned
    • These are a first cut, applied by rule to what each note records. They are not the team’s ranking and they leave out programme strategy, with one exception: schools are a programme priority, so every after-school site is set to High whatever its urgency score.
    • Priority = urgency × reach. Urgency 3: a basic service is absent, shut or unsafe (a dead RO plant, households without toilets, children in an unsafe building, an open sewer). Urgency 2: the service exists but falls short, or a specific group has none (no crèche, elderly living alone). Urgency 1: a new amenity (hall, library, park, skill centre, after-school). Reach is the population of the settlement served: under 1,000, 1,000–2,999, or 3,000 and above. High = urgency 3 with reach of 1,000+, or urgency 2 with 3,000+.
    • Feasibility is one of five states. Ready to start: a government facility already exists and needs repair, fit-out or permission to use. Buildable: land or building is confirmed as government-owned, but the work is new construction, a rebuild or an added floor. Blocked for now: the note records something to settle first (non-government owner, a competing claim or use, a pending permission, a plot too small, no water source). Not viable as proposed: private land or a closed route. No site yet: a need is recorded but no site was assessed.
    • The team’s own recommendation (Ready / Ready with conditions) is shown on each site where the register has one. It is filled for 79 of 86 register rows and never says “Not suitable”, so it does not separate sites on its own.
    • North Zone status comes from the 1 October application to the North Zone Commissioner, not from this folder.
    How the GBA proposal was derived from this assessment
    • Proposed = ready to start or buildable. The 110 entries here reduce to 71 proposed sites: blocked, not viable and no-site entries are left out (16 of them are listed in Annexure 3 as sites needing clarification), and so are the four sites whose only need was an anganwadi building, since anganwadis are run by the Department of Women and Child Development. At three other sites the anganwadi was dropped and the rest kept.
    • Crèches replace the earlier use at five sites (Ragigudda, Ittige Factory, Rasaldar Street, the Swatantra Nagar hall and the Pattankot hall), chosen because they are ground-floor buildings that meet the crèche protocols. With the three sites assessed as crèches, that makes eight.
    • Labels follow the note: crèche, livelihood centre, community resource centre, toilets / sanitation complex. Three toilet proposals (Vinobanagar, Rachenahalli, Shariff Nagara) are integrated sanitation complexes; the other seven are refurbishments.
    • Year 1 earmarks (39 facilities + 7 schools) were decided intervention by intervention on 28 October: all crèches, toilet refurbishments and the ready community resource centres, youth centres and libraries; 5 RO repairs by catchment size; 5 new RO units (the three North Zone commitments plus the two largest in Central); Rachenahalli as the first sanitation complex; Siddharth Nagar livelihood centre; Rajendra Nagar children’s centre; V S Garden park. Nothing in East.
    • Approval type follows the work: permission to repair and use for ready sites, allotment of land for new construction on vacant plots, handover of an existing building for the rest.
    • City-wide items (shelters, health, animal welfare, childcare institutions) have no settlement site; they are summarised in the GBA proposal tab. The three animal premises are plotted at approximate locations.
    Gaps and conflicts in the source documents
    • The initial assessment sheet enters two clusters twice. Its last 51 rows repeat Nagarabhavi and Nayandahalli in rougher form; they are counted once here, leaving 386 needs. Three rows marked “No need” are left out. Majestic does not appear in that sheet at all, though it has 20 assessed sites.
    • The register is incomplete. It has 86 rows against 103 site notes. Sixteen of the 18 North Zone notes and the Gangondanahalli anganwadi note are missing from it. Review, status and resource-person columns are empty throughout.
    • Zone and corporation labels disagree. Koramangala sites are filed under both Central and South; Nayandahalli and Nagarabhavi under both West and South; Yeshwanthpur notes sit in the West folder but the register puts them under the North corporation; Kengeri notes are named WZ in the folder and SZ in the detail tabs. This page uses the folder each note was filed in.
    • Coordinates need a second look at eight sites. Four were typed in degree-minute format and converted here (Maruthinagar, Bhuvaneshwarinagar, Ambedkar Quarters hall, Gangondanahalli). The Majestic school’s register coordinate (12.58317, 77.33454) is outside the city; the note’s was used. The Kengeri park note gives latitude 12.98002 against 12.917981 in the snapshot. The V S Garden RO snapshot coordinate falls in Nagarabhavi. The Lakshman Rao Nagar RO note repeats the Ambedkar Nagar 3rd Cross coordinate, and the two Koramangala repair sites are swapped in the register.
    • Population figures conflict. Ambedkar Quarters is 2,340 in two notes and 4,390 in a third. V S Garden has 1,061, 2,465 and 2,945 households in different places. Vasanthapura shows 119 households for 4,057 people. The Ragigudda notes carry V S Garden’s population (5,023). The Gopalpura RO note carries Okalipura’s figures. Ittige Factory’s age groups add up to more than its population. All four Ullalu notes use an average of six other settlements.
    • Shariff Nagara toilets: the same note says 180 and 480 households without toilets.
    • Owner is recorded differently in note and register for the Koramangala, JJR Nagar, KR Market, Kengeri RO and Ullalu sites (BBMP, Slum Board, BDA and BWSSB appear for the same plots).
    • The Kottigepalya note is out of date. It still says “Not confirmed (stop)”; ownership was later confirmed as BBMP and the site is in the North Zone application.
    • Mislabels. The Gas Godown kitchen note names its canteen Kodigehalli, but it is the Sanjay Nagar Ward 19 canteen. Community Center 06 (Gopalpura) describes Srirampura in its text. The Majestic register rows have shifted columns, so asks sit in the households column. The Majestic school contact number has eight digits. The Thilaknagar snapshot row is labelled library but describes a park.
    • Several settlements have two proposals for the same thing: two RO sites in Ambedkar Nagar (Koramangala), two halls each in Srirampura and Swatantra Nagar, and two notes for one yard at Rachenahalli.
    • Officials’ phone numbers are left off this page. Names and designations are shown; the numbers are in the notes.
    Where the settlement footprints and the basemap come from
    • The shaded polygons are the programme’s own settlement mapping: 298 settlements across 20 clusters in four zones, drawn settlement by settlement by nine partner teams (Sangama, CFAR, ActionAid, Gubbachi, SIEDS, Janashayog, Maarga, Thamate, Sama) and kept current as they work. Each footprint is coloured by the partner that works there. The small blue squares are the 28 resource centres the programme already runs. Snapshot of 28 October 2026.
    • The overlay is matched spatially, not by name. 50 of the 103 geocoded assessment sites fall inside a mapped footprint and 91 sit in or within 200 m of one; 34 mapped settlements hold at least one assessed site. Settlement names are spelled differently between the assessment notes and the mapping, so the position on the ground, not the name, links the two.
    • Zones differ from city corporations. The footprints carry the programme’s zones (Central, West, North, South); the assessment sites are placed in the GBA city corporations notified in November 2025. The two mostly coincide but are not the same boundaries.
    • Some mapped clusters are outside the opening frame. Anekal, Bagalur, Sarjapur Road and Bellandur lie beyond it — zoom out to reach them. They had no sites in this assessment round.
